title: Do you carry too much for everyone else?
intro: Some people become overwhelmed not because they aren't strong — but because they've spent too long carrying everything alone. People-pleasing and overfunctioning can make it difficult to recognize your own limits, needs, and exhaustion. This check-in is designed to help you understand how emotional overgiving may currently be affecting you.

options.text: Uncomfortable when people are upset with me
Emotionally responsible for others
Worried about disappointing people
Exhausted from constantly giving to others
Disconnected from my own needs and limits

questions.text: When people need help, I usually:

options.text: Avoid saying no to keep the peace
Take on their emotions as my own
Want reassurance that I'm helping enough
Give more than I realistically can
Put their needs before mine automatically
I try too hard to avoid conflict
I carry too much emotional weight for others
I rely heavily on external validation
I've been emotionally overextending myself
I rarely prioritize myself fully

questions.text: People around me probably see me as:

options.text: Easygoing and accommodating
Emotionally supportive
Caring and approval-seeking
Always available to help
Selfless and dependable

questions.text: What do you need most right now?

options.text: Healthier boundaries around conflict
Emotional separation from other people's stress
Reassurance from yourself instead of others
Time to recover and recharge
Permission to prioritize yourself too

a.description: You avoid conflict, tension, or disappointing others in order to keep things calm. Your need for harmony often comes at the cost of your own honest expression.

b.description: You feel responsible for managing or carrying other people's emotions. You absorb what others feel and often lose track of what you feel yourself.

c.description: You look for reassurance, validation, or external approval to feel secure. Your sense of worth is tied closely to how others respond to you.

d.description: You give too much emotionally, mentally, or physically without enough recovery. Your generosity is real — but it's depleting you.

e.description: You consistently ignore personal needs, limits, or emotional well-being for others. You have become so focused on others that you've lost touch with yourself.
